ashok: Heads-up — after enabling torch.compile + CUDA graphs on prod pool, we've seen kernel choices shift for seqlen 1024 workloads. Latency tail increased ~25%. Dumped profiler; suspect capture is freezing kernel selection that autotuner expects.

maria: can you paste the profile and repro steps?

ashok: sure

ashok: ```
# sample kernel timeline (from nvprof/RuntimeTrace)
0.0s fused_gemm_v2_sm80     42.3%
0.0s gemm_fp16_sm80         17.1%
0.0s softmax_opt_sm80       12.5%
0.0s fused_gemm_v1_sm75     26.2%  # previously dominant on same model
```

ashok: note: with torch.compile off we saw fused_gemm_v1_sm75 dominate; with compile+cudagraphs capture picks v2.

jordan: my hunch — graph capture sees a shorter live shape during KV prefill and pins a kernel that is suboptimal for final steady-state length. Also autotuner run-time hook might be skipped once a static graph exists.

maria: that matches the perf regression traces we saw last week where warmup bias changed the kernel histogram. KV cache prefill path uses smaller batch sizes and short seq.

ashok: REPRO:
```
python -m runtime.bench --model redwood-xl --seq 1024 --compile --cudagraphs --warmup 32 --kv-prefill 16
```

maria: quick check — can you force a full autotune after graph capture? e.g. set RUNTIME_AUTOTUNE_FORCE=1 and rerun capture.

jordan: also try `--cudagraphs=capture_templates` flag to capture multiple templates, or disable capture for warmup loop only.

runtime-bench: Scheduled bench job #4872 for ashok on staging (seqlen=1024, compile=true, cudagraphs=templates)

ashok: noted. I'll run with AUTOTUNE_FORCE and post results. If kernel mismatch persists, we should add a capture-hook to re-run kernel selection after KV prefill, or add a policy to prefer backward-compatible kernels for captured graphs.

maria: agree. If you get numbers, attach pico-profile + kernel histogram. quick diff between before/after autotune will be helpful.

ashok: will do. ETA ~2h. thanks :thumbsup:
